name: HashiCorp
look: Black canvas throughout with a per-product colour identity, tight display against relaxed body, and hairlines felt more than seen.

hero.title: Provision, secure and run any infrastructure
hero.sub: Seven products that each do one thing properly, with a shared workflow across every cloud you happen to be on.

features.title: Seven products, one workflow
features.sub: Each carries its own colour identity, and each replaces a category of bespoke scripts.

items.title: Provision
items.body: Declarative infrastructure across three thousand providers, with a plan you review before anything changes.

items.title: Secrets
items.body: Dynamic, short-lived credentials issued on request instead of long-lived keys in a config file.

items.title: Service mesh
items.body: Service discovery, mTLS and traffic policy across clusters and clouds.

items.title: Scheduling
items.body: One scheduler for containers, virtual machines and plain binaries.

items.title: Access
items.body: Identity-based access to hosts and databases, with every session recorded.

items.title: Images
items.body: Reproducible machine images built once and promoted through environments.

showcases.title: The plan is the product
showcases.body: Every change is proposed as a plan before it is applied. Reviewing a diff of infrastructure changes turns a risky operation into an ordinary code review, which is the whole reason the category exists.
points: Plan reviewed before any change is applied

showcases.title: Credentials that expire on their own
showcases.body: Instead of a long-lived key sitting in an environment variable, a service requests a credential when it needs one and that credential expires shortly afterwards. Leaked secrets stop being an emergency.

gallery.title: DOCUMENTATION
gallery.sub: Tutorials, references and reference architectures for each product.

testimonial.quote: We deleted eleven thousand lines of bash. The scripts had worked, technically, but nobody could tell you what state the account was actually in.
testimonial.name: Karl Bergman

pricing.title: PRICING
pricing.sub: Open source is free. Cloud is priced per resource under management.

items.a: The core of every product is open under MPL 2.0 with no feature gating. The paid tiers add governance, managed state and support rather than capability.

items.q: Do the products require each other?
items.a: No. Each is usable on its own, and most teams adopt one first. They share a workflow and an identity model when you do run several.
All the major ones, plus three thousand community providers covering everything from DNS registrars to SaaS tools.
Stored, versioned and locked so two engineers cannot apply conflicting changes. Self-managed users choose their own backend; Cloud manages it for you.

cta.title: Start with one product
cta.sub: Free and open source, or try the managed workflow.

footer.tagline: Provision, secure and run any infrastructure.

notes: The black canvas carries hero, body, pricing, comparison tables and footer alike — there is no light interlude.
Each product owns a colour identity with its own button and card variant. Mixing two product colours in one component breaks the system.
The typographic voice is the proportional gap: display at tight 1.17–1.21 line-height, body in the same family at a relaxed 1.5–1.7.
CTAs sit at 8px, not pills, which keeps the system reading as developer-tool rather than consumer app.
Elevation is a charcoal surface lift rather than shadow, and 1px translucent hairlines define cards — felt more than seen.
